feedback.problem:
Complete the following parametric equations generating the hyperbola $16{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2}=64$ in terms of the parameter $t,$ defined for $t\in [-\pi ,\pi ]$ where $t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.$

$x=$
{{field-1}}$,\,y=4\operatorname{tan}⁡t$
feedback.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a horizontal hyperbola with Cartesian equation

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by

$$
x=a\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=b\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$

First, we rewrite the equation of our hyperbola in standard form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}16{x}^{2}-4{y}^{2} & =64 \\ \frac{16{x}^{2}}{64}-\frac{4{y}^{2}}{64} & =1 \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{4}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{16} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, in our case, we have $a=\sqrt{4}=2$ and $b=\sqrt{16}=4.$ Therefore, the parametric equations are

$$
x=2\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,y=4\operatorname{tan}⁡t.
$$
